name: safe-deploy-rollback-p1
prompt: how can I ship a release and undo it fast if error rates spike after it goes out

chunks.content: every admin change is written to an append-only audit log
we deploy the new version onto an idle stack and only flip the load balancer to it once health checks pass, so reverting is just pointing traffic back at the still-warm old stack
the release first takes one percent of traffic while we watch error rate and latency; if either crosses the threshold the pipeline automatically shifts everyone back to the prior build
config reloads on signal without dropping in-flight requests
rebuilt the settings page layout with a responsive grid and removed three dead stylesheets
the failed migration was reverted by running its down step, which dropped the half-added column and restored the previous schema
outbound notifications are queued and sent by a background worker so the web tier stays responsive
below-the-fold images now lazy-load to improve first paint
each build is an immutable, versioned artifact, so going back to the last good release is redeploying a known tag rather than rebuilding from source
a release dashboard overlays the deploy marker on the error-rate graph so spikes line up with rollouts
switched the activity list to keyset pagination using the last seen id
timestamps are stored in UTC and rendered in the viewer's local zone
if any step of the order placement fails the whole database transaction rolls back so we never half-charge a customer
